### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx`  _(via formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_
- `content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx`  _(via formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_
- `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx`  _(via formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via emptyState (literal, a string literal in ObjectTranslationDataSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via emptyState (literal, a string literal in ObjectTranslationDataSchema), formViews (literal, a string literal in collectViewRecord))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `483b10b24b4a67930c9dc84c96f29c089a0db0c2` — the merge of head `6f43b6b2e08d7e8f0a57b1bfd3213f3911c90602` into base `601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 483b10b24b4a67930c9dc84c96f29c089a0db0c2 && git checkout 483b10b24b4a67930c9dc84c96f29c089a0db0c2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103 6f43b6b2e08d7e8f0a57b1bfd3213f3911c90602 && git checkout -B drift-repro 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103 && git merge --no-ff 6f43b6b2e08d7e8f0a57b1bfd3213f3911c90602

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f43b6b2e08d7e8f0a57b1bfd3213f3911c90602`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts, .changeset/24969-form-view-title-translation-key.md, content/docs/references/system/translation.mdx, examples/app-showcase/src/system/translations/index.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (cited, unchanged)

Reviewed against card #24969 (body, claim 6303839918, dev report 6307030278), standing ruling 「甲」 (#6015 comments 6292005854 and 6303865025), the PR body and file list, the three-dot diff `origin/main...6f43b6b2e0` (13 files, +833/-17), and the head's check-runs. Read-only: no checkout, build, test or gate re-run.

**Check-runs on the head at the time of this record:** 40 runs, 0 red. 33 completed (25 success, 8 skipped by their own filters: Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke). 7 still in progress: Test Core (1/6 through 6/6) and Type Check · workspace. Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Build Core are green. The verdict below is conditional on none of the 7 pending runs going red; a red there is to be named and this record re-read.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **A separate key `objects.OBJECT._views.VIEW.title`, not the `label` key — justified.** Read in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`: `FormViewSchema` declares `title` ("Form title") and no `label`; the `ViewItem` union has exactly two arms, `list` and `form`, and `ListViewSchema` carries no top-level `title`. So a container's `formViews.KEY` / `form` entry has one string (`title`) and a `viewKind: 'form'` item can author two (`label` names the view, `config.title` is the heading). One translation standing for two source strings would be wrong whenever the two differ. The new key sits in the same `_views` node under the same view key `lookupViewText` already reads for `label` / `description`, so it is one address convention, not a second one. The `title -> label` alias removed from the `_views` entry was a refusal hint on a strict object (the new spec test shows `heading` is still refused with a rename hint), so no bundle could legally carry `_views.VIEW.title` before this PR: the key is new, nothing valid today is renamed or reshaped. `heading` and `formTitle` are added as refusal hints onto `title`; the entry stays closed.

2. **`translateView` overlay on `config.title` — correct and bounded.** `translateFormTitle` returns the input by identity when the title is not a non-empty string (so a form without a title gains none and `config` keeps its reference), when `valueOverridesPackagedBase(packagedConfig, 'title', title)` says the served title was edited on top of the package (ADR-0029 D9.2a, the same rule `label` / `description` / bulk-action defs / sections use), or when no locale on the chain carries the key. The read is through the one `lookupViewText`, widened to `'title'`. Observation, not a defect: the overlay is applied wherever `config` is an object, not only when `viewKind === 'form'`; because only `FormViewSchema` carries a top-level `title`, a list view's `config.title` is always `undefined` and the read is a no-op there, so the resolver and the lint refusal agree on the authored surface. The spec tests pin the translated title, the fallback chain, a missing key, a form with no title, the no-leak between `label` and `title`, the override rule and non-mutation.

3. **`/forms/:slug` — what an existing client receives, judged.** Before: `label: match.view?.label ?? match.form?.label` (untranslated) and `form.title` as authored. After: `form.title` is the translated title (the route already served the translated view's `config` when `match.form === match.view.config`), and `label` is `view.label` from the translated view only when `match.view.label !== undefined` (the translator always sets `label`, falling back to the machine name, so the second guard `view.label !== undefined` is always true; the effective condition is "the view authors a label"). For a container form (no authored `label`) the answer is unchanged: `label` absent, `form.title` now translated. For a `viewKind: 'form'` item that authors a `label`, a non-default-locale client now receives the translated label where it received the authored one. For a default-locale or `en` request every field is served as authored. The console's `payload.label ?? form.title ?? objectSchema.label` fall-through order is untouched and all three arms now arrive translated. This is the card's asked-for change and a widening: a client sees a translated string where it saw the authoring-language one; the shape of the response, its keys and the fallback order do not move. The REST test runs the real route over a real `SchemaRegistry` and `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` and covers translated, `en`, missing key, no title, machine-name-not-served, overlay override, and the authored-label item via a protocol double.

4. **Lint acceptance / refusal — no narrowing of anything valid today.** `facts.forms` registers `formViews.KEY` (by registry key, as `views` already does), the default form (by the composer's own runtime key via `expandViewContainer(...).find(isDefault)`, the same discipline as `defaultListViewKey`), and a `viewKind: 'form'` item. A `title` tail over a name in `views` but not in `forms` (a list view) is `translation-target-unknown` with a one-line verdict and a fix hint pointing at `_views.VIEW.label`; the entry is then skipped, so a list view's own `label` key on the same entry is still accepted (CONTROL test present). Nothing valid today is refused: the spec schema refused `_views.*.title` before this PR, so the lint refusal only names, with a better message, a key that was already illegal. The default form's key becomes legal for `title` alone; its other tails stay non-keys (test present), which is a deliberate non-widening the dev flags under ③.

5. **Extractor slot and coverage demand — acceptable.** `pushContainerFormTitles` emits `_views.KEY.title` for every form a container serves, keyed by the composer's runtime name (asked of `expandViewContainer`, never re-derived), and the `viewKind: 'form'` branch emits it for an item. `pushOptional` records a titleless form's slot without an inline value, and the CLI test shows the coverage gate reports only authored titles a supported locale leaves untranslated. The showcase authors `title: 'New contact'` on `formViews.create` with `zh-CN` supported, so the slot became a real missing translation (414 to 415); authoring `_views.create.title: '新建联系人'` in the showcase bundle is the correct way to keep the repo gate's baseline unchanged ("621 baselined, none new") rather than ratcheting the baseline. For a user app, a newly reported `i18n/missing-view` on an authored title under a supported locale is a report, not a refusal of valid metadata: the key did not exist to be demanded before, and the demand follows from the author's own `supportedLocales` declaration. Docs regenerated (`translation.mdx`, the four `_views` rows and the per-view table).

### ② Semver level

Changeset declares `minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/cli`, all at 18.0.0, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the changeset and the PR body. That matches what publishes: spec gains an optional key on a strict entry and a resolver that overlays it (additive); rest serves translated values in a response of unchanged shape (additive); lint names a refusal for a key that was already refused at parse (no narrowing); cli emits a new extractor slot (additive). No `BREAKING` shape is owed. Standing ruling 「甲」 as amended (6303865025) governs narrowings in 18.x and does not bear on this widening; the claim's `Responsibility: n/a — a widening` line is consistent with it. Semver judgment: `minor`, as declared. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev's out-of-scope notes (report 6307030278, PR Acceptance notes), none a blocker, inference not measured, no shipped example reaches them: (a) a `formViews.KEY` that retargets another object via its own `data.object` is keyed by lint under the form's binding but by `translateView` and the extractor under the container object; the `label` key already has the same split. (b) A `viewKind: 'form'` item's spec-qualified `OBJECT.KEY` name is used raw by the extractor's `view.name` branch and by lint, while `translateView` strips the prefix; the title slot inherits that branch's existing behaviour. (c) The default form's `_views.form.label` / `description` are read by `translateView` but stay lint non-keys; this PR registers `title` only. Flagged for a carrier if one is ever needed; not for this PR.
- `FormViewSchema.title`'s own `.describe()` does not name the key; the translation face documents it. Flag only.
- Stale PR-body sentence: in Tests, Derived gates, the body still reads "`pnpm check:type-check-debt` is NOT MEASURED" (lock queue timeout). The dev report says it was re-run under the lock after the PR opened, exit 0, 117 of 117, and asks the seat to correct the body. The head's `Type Check · debt ledger` check-run is green, which corroborates. Flag only: the body line is stale and is the seat's to correct; it does not change the verdict.
- 7 check-runs were still in progress when this record was rendered (Test Core 1/6 to 6/6, Type Check · workspace). None red. A red among them would be named and this record re-read.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24969-form-view-title-key`
Reviewed-by: `session_01D6F9axfoPzR7t8G1J7Ytzz`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**Seat re-read of the check-runs at landing:** all 42 runs on `6f43b6b2e0` have completed: 36 succeeded, the rest were skipped, and none is red.
